_comment: Guided tour of the channel definition tool. Targets are the toolbar controls drawn by the app (item_rects names).

steps.title: Choose or start a setup
steps.text: The Setup choice lists the saved detector setups. Pick one and its detectors, PIE windows, reading routine, LUTs and optical setup replace the working definition. Unsaved is a definition with no name.

await.hint: Pick a setup, or skip this step if none is saved yet.

steps.title: Tabs: reading, detectors, windows
steps.text: Below the toolbar the editor has six tabs. TTTR reading takes timing from a measurement; Detectors and PIE windows hold the routing channels and the micro-time ranges. Click a tab to look at it; nothing changes until you edit a field.

steps.title: Save under a name
steps.text: Save asks for a name and stores everything under it. A saved setup is what the analysis tools select.

steps.title: Name it
steps.text: Type a name and confirm. A name already in use is overwritten.

await.hint: Press Save in the prompt, or Cancel.

steps.title: Share it
steps.text: Public makes the saved setup visible to every user of the MMFDB the next time you press Save. It is available only for a saved setup you own.

steps.title: Calibration snapshots
steps.text: Every archived G-factor calibration of the selected setup is a dated snapshot. Choosing one applies its G factor, l1 and l2 to the detectors. Latest leaves them as they are.

steps.title: Rename and delete
steps.text: Rename and Delete act on the selected saved setup and ask before changing anything.

steps.title: Help
steps.text: Help explains the six tabs, the units of micro-time ranges and the LUT handling.
